scales.question: How do the three nodes connect to the regional rail, bus and public-space backbone?
Where do enterprise windows meet resident return routes and maintenance edges?
Can a node keep an ordinary route, an accessible route and a staffed handoff visible together?
Can curb, crossing, waiting, appeal and blackout states be separated in section?
scales.evidence: relative section logic, pending engineering review

scales.question: Can a public receipt, human takeover and removable interface be read at the edge?
scales.evidence: material and service detail, pending professional review

alternatives.label: enterprise-first shared curb
alternatives.reason: A single priority window lets enterprise arrival and loading occupy the same edge as ordinary and accessible movement.
alternatives.spatial_move: one shared curb with a digital priority queue

alternatives.label: three independent windows
alternatives.reason: Separate windows reduce direct conflict but split maintenance, appeal and blackout responsibilities across the three nodes.
alternatives.resident_return: ordinary route retained, shared closeout unclear
alternatives.spatial_move: three local windows without a common receipt

alternatives.label: reciprocal node chain
alternatives.reason: The enterprise request, resident return, human handoff and public closeout stay paired at every node while the digital or feeder layer remains removable.
alternatives.resident_return: ordinary, accessible, rail-bus and staffed routes remain first-class
alternatives.spatial_move: three nodes with one shared receipt grammar and independent maintenance edges

rights_matrix.ordinary_service: continuous accessible route and human help
rights_matrix.enterprise_condition: no longer or less safe route
